claim: The people stand at a distance in fear; Moses tells them not to fear in one sense and says God has come to test them so that his fear may be before them and they may not sin.
label: Fear at the manifestation and Moses' explanation

claim: Moses reports Yahweh's words, the people promise obedience, Moses reads the book of the covenant, and blood is applied as he identifies the covenant Yahweh made with them.
label: Book and blood of the covenant

claim: Yahweh calls Moses up for stone tablets; Moses enters the cloud, and the text states he is on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
label: Tablets and forty days on the mountain

claim: While Moses delays, the people seek gods; Aaron makes a calf; later Aaron tells Moses a version of events that includes the claim that the calf came out of the fire.
label: Golden calf and Aaron's explanation

claim: Moses returns to Yahweh, acknowledges the people's great sin, asks concerning forgiveness and being blotted from God's book, and Yahweh answers concerning judgment.
label: Moses intercedes after the calf

claim: Moses asks for God's presence and glory; the chapter also says Yahweh spoke with Moses 'face to face' while later stating that no one can see God's face and live.
label: Presence, glory, and the face-language boundary

claim: Moses receives replacement tablets, Yahweh proclaims his name/character, covenant commands are renewed, Moses again spends forty days and nights, and his face shines after speaking with Yahweh.
label: New tablets, name proclamation, covenant renewal, and shining face

claim: Yahweh rejects judging by outward appearance, directs Samuel to David, and David is anointed among his brothers.
label: David is chosen and anointed

claim: After Samuel anoints David, the narrator says the Spirit of Yahweh comes mightily on David from that day forward.
label: Spirit of Yahweh comes on David

claim: The narrative says the Spirit of Yahweh departed from Saul and describes Saul's distress; David is brought into Saul's service and plays the lyre when Saul is troubled.
label: David serves Saul with music

claim: Goliath challenges Israel; David hears the challenge, asks about it, and tells Saul he will go fight the Philistine.
label: Goliath's challenge and David volunteers

claim: David tells Goliath he comes in Yahweh's name and says the battle is Yahweh's and the assembly will know Yahweh does not save with sword and spear.
label: David says the battle belongs to Yahweh

claim: David runs toward Goliath, strikes him with a stone from the sling, Goliath falls, and David then uses Goliath's own sword.
label: David defeats Goliath with sling and stone

claim: David has an opportunity against Saul, cuts the edge of Saul's robe, refuses to strike Yahweh's anointed, and later addresses Saul about his restraint.
label: David spares Saul

claim: Israel's tribes come to David at Hebron; the elders make a covenant with him and anoint him king; the text states he is thirty when he begins to reign and reigns forty years.
label: David is anointed king over Israel

claim: David captures the stronghold of Zion/Jerusalem, builds there, and the narrator says he knows Yahweh has established him as king and exalted his kingdom for Israel's sake.
label: Jerusalem captured and David established

claim: Through Nathan, Yahweh promises David a great name, rest, a house/dynasty, an offspring after him, and a kingdom/throne described as established forever.
label: Oracle of house, offspring, kingdom, and throne

claim: David sends for Bathsheba, sleeps with her, arranges Uriah's death after her pregnancy is reported, later takes her as wife, and the narrator says what David did displeased Yahweh.
label: David, Bathsheba, Uriah, and narrator judgment

claim: Nathan tells a parable, identifies David as the man, announces consequences, David says he has sinned against Yahweh, and Nathan responds that Yahweh has put away his sin while consequences remain.
label: Nathan confronts David
